title: U.S. Navy Picks Blue Water Autonomy for Deep-Ocean Survey Ships
summary: Blue Water Autonomy said on August 4, 2026 that the U.S. Navy selected it under a multi-year, multiple-award IDIQ contract with a $40 million ceiling to run autonomous vessels on deep-ocean survey missions. The ships will produce high-resolution seafloor mapping across the Indian and Pacific oceans, gathering terrain, acoustic and operating-condition data. Its Liberty Class vessel is a 190-foot steel ship built on Damen's Stan Patrol 6009 hull, with over 10,000 nautical miles of range and more than 150 metric tons of payload, and integrates hardware, software and AI in one stack. The company, founded in 2024, expects to finish its first Navy vessel this year under an existing program of record; it has raised $64 million in total, including a $50 million Series A.
whyItMatters: Autonomy at sea is judged on endurance rather than dexterity: a 10,000-nautical-mile unmanned survey ship has to hold its own perception, navigation and fault handling for weeks with no one aboard and no reliable link home. Winning a program-of-record slot two years after founding shows the Navy is now buying autonomy from startups on the same footing as established shipbuilders, and ocean-floor mapping is the low-risk mission where that trust gets established before higher-stakes ones follow.
